summary:
# NOTES: "Just a Girl" by Charles Garvice (Gutenberg #57166, 1895)

Single book, no BOOK headings. Chapters I–XLIV plus a Transcriber's note at the end.

## Setting / cast
- **Three Star Camp**, Australian gold camp, Wally River valley. Saloon: **Eldorado** (owner **Dan MacGrath**, infamous whisky). Nearby rival camp: **Dog's Ear** (its men: Simon, Scraggy-head/Edward, a burly one-armed leader). Other camps: Good Luck, Ballarat, Wally-Wally, Melbourne.
- **Varley Howard**: gambler, languid, white hands, diamond ring/scarf-pin, tall silk hat, mustache, quotes "Olivette"; deadliest shot. Guardian of Esmeralda. Calls ward "Ralda."
- **Esmeralda** (Ralda): foundling, ~3 when found; red-gold/auburn hair, dark brown eyes, freckles, large mouth, expressive; rides, shoots, swims Wally River, tracks. Named at Eldorado (Esmeralda Howard) by the doctor's suggestion.
- **Bill the postman** (Willyum): found her on road 3 miles from Dog's Ear beside dead woman; brought her in mail-sack. Mare (shies). Huge mouth. Has a head wound later.
- **Mother Melinda**: old woman who raised Esmeralda; hut.
- **Taffy**: Welshman, giant dare-devil, drunk comic; bought satin cradle; gave Esmeralda note at parting.
- **The Penman**: shaky schoolmaster, taught Esmeralda; "Yesterday she hit me with the grammar."
- **Dr. / "the Parson"**: doctor who read funeral service; treated Norman.
- **Smifkens**: baronet at camp. **Polly**, black-eyed; Mary Anne; "Barber's Block" anecdote.
- **Lord Norman Druce** ("Pink Rosebud" to camp), of The Manor, Oakfield; cousin of Trafford; mother Lady Druce. Shot in calf by Dog's Ear man when defending a dog; Esmeralda removed bullet (she keeps it). Sings tenor; proposes by moonlight at river; she refuses. Gives her a locket later. Later loves Lilias.
- **Trafford** = Lord Trafford, Marquis of Trafford, eldest son of **Duke of Belfayre** (old, kind, white-haired; "my dear"). Lives in the Albany; club Marlborough; dark, grave, tall; black pearl shirt stud. Heir with cash crisis; wants "to marry money." Father duke dies suddenly night of Esmeralda's flight.
- **Lord Selvaine**: Trafford's uncle, bachelor, thin, gray, womanish hands, cynical, master-mind of family; "The woman who hesitates is won."
- **Lilias Selvaine**: Selvaine's niece, 19, small, dark hair, soft blue-gray eyes; runs Belfayre; loves Norman.
- **Lady Ada Lancing**: fair, blue eyes, "daughter of the gods," Scotch peer's daughter, poor; Trafford's former love; guardian Lady Grange. Hates Esmeralda; forges plot (keeps Norman's letter, "I can not stay here now that there is no hope...").
- **Lady Wyndover**: Esmeralda's guardian in London; flaxen dyed hair, rouge, thin voice; Deepdale (Surrey) cottage; maid **Barker** (dislikes Esmeralda's ways). Footman Thomas.
- **Mr. Samson Pinchook**, solicitor, Pinchook, Pinchook & Becham, 119 Grey's Inn; executor for **Gordon Chetwynde** (millionaire, >£2 million); Esmeralda is granddaughter; mother Mrs. Chetwynde (née Chetwynde) died in Australia.
- **Madame Cerise** (Irish-French dressmaker, Mount Street).
- Others: **Lord Blankyre** & Lady Blankyre (party hostess, white velvet); **Lord Villiers** ball; **Lord Dunworthy** (Irish viscount); **Lord Chesterleigh** & daughter **Lady Mary**; **Lady Desford**; **Mr. Elmbourne** (PM); **Mr. Helby** (steward); **Ffoulkes** (best man); **Lord Grange**; Prince of Seidlitzberg; bishop; **Millais** (portrait).

## Key events in order
1. Eldorado row; Bill brings baby in mail-sack; Varley wins child by cards ("an ace"). Named Esmeralda; "Esmeralda! And luck to her!"
2. Camp adores her: satin cradle, measles, riding, shooting. Penman's lessons; Varley: "chuck it" joke; "I'm your guardian... princess in disguise"; "I shall marry you"—"I think not."
3. Norman rescued by Esmeralda in wood (hat shot through, she kills a Dog's Ear man). Card: "Lord Norman Druce, The Manor, Oakfield."
4. Norman at camp; Taffy names him Pink Rosebud. Delirium: he calls "Ralda"; mentions "Trafford" and "Ada." Moonlight river: Norman confesses love; Esmeralda says "No."
5. Pinchook arrives; Varley explains inheritance; Esmeralda "I shall not go without Varley"; Varley's bargain: come back if unhappy. Camp send-off with concertina ("Auld Lang Syne", "God Save the Queen"). Note from Norman: "I must go on loving you till I die."
6. London: Lady Wyndover; Madame Cerise; Barker; Lady Blankyre's party (Lord Selvaine; meets Trafford). Esmeralda saves Lady Ada's horse in Rotten Row. Trafford dances with her, Lady Ada confronts Esmeralda.
7. Trafford proposes in carriage (Shirley/West Wickham drive); "Yes" in Belfayre. Belfayre visit; duke's lake story (Trafford ancestor's wife suicide). Stables; orchid; Lilias.
8. Engagement; Lady Mary jealousy; horse falls at gate; Trafford proposes again; "Yes, I love you"—they kiss. Pinchook: settlements. Wedding at church; Ada's bridesmaid; Ada overhears in anteroom; Norman's telegram.
9. Honeymoon at Deepdale; ring left; night quarrel; Esmeralda's "No!" Trafford sleeps out. Belfayre return; Norman/Trafford/Ada tensions; Ada plants letter; dinner party; fernery: Trafford sees Norman kiss Esmeralda; Trafford accuses; Esmeralda leaves at night, visits duke's room (kiss; tear), walks out past Trafford's sleep.
10. Duke dies. Trafford lies about Esmeralda being "at Deepdale." Norman telegram; sails for Australia. Trafford follows on "Trafford" ship; Norman books berths.
11. Three Star: Dog's Ear robbery of coach (Johnson driver, Varley saves passengers, Esmeralda recognised on coach; she rides behind Varley). Esmeralda kidnapped by Simon; ransom £200 by Friday at Raven Claim. Esmeralda escapes with woman's help (revolver). Varley rides to Wally-Wally, gets £160 gold.
12. Trafford meets Varley at Raven Claim; duel; Esmeralda flings herself between; Varley's shot wounds her shoulder; Trafford's arm wounded; doctor saves her. Trafford confesses to Varley; Norman explains; Varley's questions expose Lady Ada.
13. Recovery; reconciliation in hammock ("Forgive me"; "I have always loved you"). Selvaine cover story; Lilias/Norman engaged; honeymoon at Three Star; Varley and Lady Ada: "She will never come back." THE END.

## Quoted refrains
"Esmeralda! And luck to her!"; "Pink Rosebud"; "Chuck it"; "I can not stay here now that there is no hope for me...I must go on loving you till I die. NORMAN."; "Take her and be happy."; "Don't you think you had better come back now?"

## Transcriber's notes
Spaced mdash retained; some pg typo fixes (e.g. Wyndham→Wyndover, Ida→Ada).
